text:
sasha: quick heads-up, ran a quick drop-in of llm.int8 (bitsandbytes) against aurora-13b on our regtest slice and seeing a consistent quality delta on summarization tasks :frowning:

maya: how big a delta?

sasha: about 2.3 ROUGE-L absolute down vs fp16 on the long-doc slice (seq 2048). throughput looks great though, ~1.9x tokens/sec.

ravi: can you paste the exact eval command you used?

sasha: sure:
```
python eval.py --model aurora-13b --quantize llm.int8 --bnb-version 0.39 --batch 8 --seq 2048 --slice long-docs
```

toni: any config flags for offload or nf4? last time nf4 helped some failure modes.

sasha: default llm.int8 loader, no NF4. eval-bot posted run summary:
```
metric: ROUGE-L
fp16: 47.0
int8: 44.7 (-2.3)
perplexity (lm): fp16 12.4 -> int8 14.1
throughput: fp16 27.8 toks/s -> int8 52.4 toks/s (+1.88x)
p95 latency: fp16 110ms -> int8 190ms (tail moved up, likely CPU offload spikes)
```

maya: interesting, perf win but tail latency up and quality down on long contexts. could be KV-cache numeric drift or layernorm precision in weight-only path.

ravi: does the drop show up on short-form QA/sanitation slices?

sasha: no, short QA and synth-instruct slice are within noise (~0.2). it's mostly long-document summarization and some codegen edge cases.

toni: steps: 1) rerun with nf4 quantization flag, 2) try bnb 0.38 vs 0.39, 3) run with small lr-scale/quantize-stable flags if supported, 4) compare against GPTQ/AWQ for the same model.

maya: I'll spin up 3 jobs: nf4, bnb=0.38, and the same with cpu_offload=False. putting them in staging canary group.

deploy-bot: canary deploy request accepted: aurora-13b-int8-canary -> staging (3 jobs) by maya at 1767002200

eval-bot: job 1 (nf4) complete:
```
ROUGE-L: 46.1 (+1.4 vs int8 default, -0.9 vs fp16)
throughput: 49.8 toks/s
```

ravi: nf4 recovered a lot, nice. what's the memory/infra delta?

sasha: nf4 increases CPU decode cost slightly but still within Dedicated capacity. memory reduced further vs default int8.

maya: job 2 (bnb 0.38) result:
```
ROUGE-L: 45.6 (-0.9 vs fp16, +0.9 vs int8 default)
throughput: 50.1 toks/s
```

toni: so older bnb helps some. could be a change in quantization rounding in 0.39. we'll file a reproducible micro-batch to isolate.

sasha: I also ran a quick gradient-check style probe (no training, just forward differences) and saw layernorm scale shifts in layers 18-22 under int8 path. attaching short dump in thread.

ravi: next actions?

maya: 1) pin bnb 0.38 for aurora-13b-int8 in Dedicated for now, 2) add nf4 as optional config for long-doc workloads in the console, 3) open an upstream issue with bitsandbytes linking our minimal repro and layer dumps, 4) schedule a short bakeoff comparing weight-only int8 vs GPTQ 8-bit on the long-doc slice.

sasha: +1. I'll prepare the repro and add eval prompts and seeds.

toni: add a quick A/B route in the router to fallback to fp16 for requests with seq > 1536 until we confirm safety. low effort fix.

maya: created issue: https://our.internal/issue/INF-2143 referencing bnb 0.39 regressions and attached dumps.

eval-bot: scheduled GPTQ job (queued) at 1767005000

ravi: thanks folks. this looks actionable. if A/B shows fp16 wins on long docs we should default long-doc routes to nf4 or fp16 until we have a robust int8 profile. :thumbsup:

sasha: agreed. I'll update the PR for deployment defaults and link this thread.

deploy-bot: canary rollback ticket created in case of regressions at 1767007000

maya: final note — please add any customer repros to the issue, especially ones with user prompts + expected summaries. that will help debugging and triage. :eyes:
